passages.text: On the third day David and his men arrived in Ziklag, and the Amalekites had raided the Negev, attacked Ziklag, and burned it down.
passages.sermon:
David was the leader of his men.
David and his men traveled together.
On the third day, David and his men arrived at Ziklag.
The Amalekites were enemies of David and his people.
The Amalekites had raided the Negev.
The Amalekites had also attacked Ziklag.
The Amalekites struck Ziklag.
The Amalekites burned Ziklag with fire.
passages.original: וַיְהִ֞י בְּבֹ֨א דָוִ֧ד וַאֲנָשָׁ֛יו צִֽקְלַ֖ג בַּיּ֣וֹם הַשְּׁלִישִׁ֑י וַעֲמָלֵקִ֣י פָֽשְׁט֗וּ אֶל־ נֶ֙גֶב֙ וְאֶל־ צִ֣קְלַ֔ג וַיַּכּוּ֙ אֶת־ צִ֣קְלַ֔ג וַיִּשְׂרְפ֥וּ אֹתָ֖הּ בָּאֵֽשׁ׃

passages.text: They had taken captive the women and all who were there, both young and old. They had not killed anyone, but had carried them off as they went on their way.
passages.sermon:
The Amalekites attacked Ziklag.
They took captive everyone in the city.
They captured all the women.
They captured all the people, both young and old.
They did not kill anyone.
They led the captives away.
They went on their way with the captives.
passages.original: וַיִּשְׁבּ֨וּ אֶת־ הַנָּשִׁ֤ים אֲשֶׁר־ בָּהּ֙ מִקָּטֹ֣ן וְעַד־ גָּד֔וֹל לֹ֥א הֵמִ֖יתוּ אִ֑ישׁ וַיִּֽנְהֲג֔וּ וַיֵּלְכ֖וּ לְדַרְכָּֽם׃

passages.text: When David and his men came to the city, they found it burned down and their wives and sons and daughters taken captive.
passages.sermon:
David was the leader of his men.
David and his men returned to their city.
They entered the city.
They saw the city.
The city was burned with fire.
Their wives were not there.
Their sons were not there.
Their daughters were not there.
Enemies had taken their wives captive.
Enemies had taken their sons captive.
Enemies had taken their daughters captive.
passages.original: וַיָּבֹ֨א דָוִ֤ד וַֽאֲנָשָׁיו֙ אֶל־ הָעִ֔יר וְהִנֵּ֥ה שְׂרוּפָ֖ה בָּאֵ֑שׁ וּנְשֵׁיהֶ֛ם וּבְנֵיהֶ֥ם וּבְנֹתֵיהֶ֖ם נִשְׁבּֽוּ׃

passages.text: So David and the troops with him lifted up their voices and wept until they had no strength left to weep.
passages.sermon:
David was the leader of the people with him.
David and his men saw their city destroyed.
They saw their families taken captive.
David and his men cried out loudly.
They wept together.
They wept until they had no strength left.
They could not weep anymore.
passages.original: וַיִּשָּׂ֨א דָוִ֜ד וְהָעָ֧ם אֲשֶׁר־ אִתּ֛וֹ אֶת־ קוֹלָ֖ם וַיִּבְכּ֑וּ עַ֣ד אֲשֶׁ֧ר אֵין־ בָּהֶ֛ם כֹּ֖חַ לִבְכּֽוֹת׃

passages.text: David’s two wives, Ahinoam of Jezreel and Abigail the widow of Nabal of Carmel, had been taken captive.
passages.sermon:
David had two wives.
Their names were Ahinoam and Abigail.
Ahinoam came from Jezreel.
Abigail was the widow of Nabal from Carmel.
Enemies took both women captive.
passages.original: וּשְׁתֵּ֥י נְשֵֽׁי־ דָוִ֖ד נִשְׁבּ֑וּ אֲחִינֹ֙עַם֙ הַיִּזְרְעֵלִ֔ית וַאֲבִיגַ֕יִל אֵ֖שֶׁת נָבָ֥ל הַֽכַּרְמְלִֽי׃

passages.text: And David was greatly distressed because the people spoke of stoning him, because the soul of every man grieved for his sons and daughters. But David found strength in the LORD his God.
passages.sermon:
David was the leader of the people.
The people suffered a great loss.
Each man grieved for his sons and daughters.
The people spoke about stoning David.
David felt very distressed.
David found strength in the LORD his God.
passages.original: וַתֵּ֨צֶר לְדָוִ֜ד מְאֹ֗ד כִּֽי־ אָמְר֤וּ הָעָם֙ לְסָקְל֔וֹ כִּֽי־ מָ֙רָה֙ נֶ֣פֶשׁ כָּל־ הָעָ֔ם אִ֖ישׁ עַל־ בְּנוֹ וְעַל־ בְּנֹתָ֑יו וַיִּתְחַזֵּ֣ק דָּוִ֔ד בַּיהוָ֖ה אֱלֹהָֽיו׃ס

passages.text: Then David said to Abiathar the priest, the son of Ahimelech, “Bring me the ephod.” So Abiathar brought it to him, and David inquired of the LORD: “Should I pursue these raiders? Will I overtake them?” “Pursue them,” the LORD replied, “for you will surely overtake them and rescue the captives.”
passages.sermon:
David was the leader of the people.
Abiathar was a priest.
Abiathar was the son of Ahimelech.
David spoke to Abiathar.
David said, “Bring me the ephod.”
Abiathar brought the ephod to David.
David asked the LORD a question.
David said, “Should I pursue these raiders?”
David also asked, “Will I overtake them?”
The LORD answered David.
The LORD said, “Pursue them.”
The LORD said, “You will surely overtake them.”
The LORD said, “You will rescue the captives.”
passages.original: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר דָּוִ֗ד אֶל־ אֶבְיָתָ֤ר הַכֹּהֵן֙ בֶּן־ אֲחִימֶ֔לֶךְ הַגִּֽישָׁה־ נָּ֥א לִ֖י הָאֵפֹ֑ד וַיַּגֵּ֧שׁ אֶבְיָתָ֛ר אֶת־ הָאֵפֹ֖ד אֶל־ דָּוִֽד׃ וַיִּשְׁאַ֨ל דָּוִ֤ד בַּֽיהוָה֙ לֵאמֹ֔ר אֶרְדֹּ֛ף אַחֲרֵ֥י הַגְּדוּד־ הַזֶּ֖ה הַֽאַשִּׂגֶ֑נּוּ וַיֹּ֤אמֶר לוֹ֙ רְדֹ֔ף כִּֽי־ הַשֵּׂ֥ג תַּשִּׂ֖יג וְהַצֵּ֥ל תַּצִּֽיל׃

passages.text: So David and his six hundred men went to the Brook of Besor, where some stayed behind because two hundred men were too exhausted to cross the brook. But David and four hundred men continued in pursuit.
passages.sermon:
David was the leader of six hundred men.
David and his men traveled together.
They reached the Brook of Besor.
Some men stayed at the brook.
Two hundred men were too tired to cross the brook.
David continued with four hundred men.
David and these four hundred men pursued their enemies.
passages.original: וַיֵּ֣לֶךְ דָּוִ֗ד ה֚וּא וְשֵׁשׁ־ מֵא֥וֹת אִישׁ֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר אִתּ֔וֹ וַיָּבֹ֖אוּ עַד־ נַ֣חַל הַבְּשׂ֑וֹר וְהַנּֽוֹתָרִ֖ים עָמָֽדוּ׃ וַיִּרְדֹּ֣ף דָּוִ֔ד ה֖וּא וְאַרְבַּע־ מֵא֣וֹת אִ֑ישׁ וַיַּֽעַמְדוּ֙ מָאתַ֣יִם אִ֔ישׁ אֲשֶׁ֣ר פִּגְּר֔וּ מֵעֲבֹ֖ר אֶת־ נַ֥חַל הַבְּשֽׂוֹר׃

passages.text: Now his men found an Egyptian in the field and brought him to David. They gave the man water to drink and food to eat— a piece of a fig cake and two clusters of raisins. So he ate and was revived, for he had not had any food or water for three days and three nights.
passages.sermon:
David was the leader of his men.
David’s men found a man in a field.
This man was Egyptian.
David’s men brought the Egyptian to David.
They gave the Egyptian bread.
He ate the bread.
They gave him water.
He drank the water.
They gave him a piece of fig cake.
They gave him two clusters of raisins.
He ate the fig cake and the raisins.
The Egyptian became strong again.
He had not eaten bread for three days and three nights.
He had not drunk water for three days and three nights.
passages.original: וַֽיִּמְצְא֤וּ אִישׁ־ מִצְרִי֙ בַּשָּׂדֶ֔ה וַיִּקְח֥וּ אֹת֖וֹ אֶל־ דָּוִ֑ד וַיִּתְּנוּ־ ל֥וֹ לֶ֙חֶם֙ וַיֹּ֔אכַל וַיַּשְׁקֻ֖הוּ מָֽיִם׃ וַיִּתְּנוּ־ לוֹ֩ פֶ֨לַח דְּבֵלָ֜ה וּשְׁנֵ֤י צִמֻּקִים֙ וַיֹּ֔אכַל וַתָּ֥שָׁב רוּח֖וֹ אֵלָ֑יו כִּ֠י לֹֽא־ אָ֤כַל לֶ֙חֶם֙ וְלֹא־ שָׁ֣תָה מַ֔יִם שְׁלֹשָׁ֥ה יָמִ֖ים וּשְׁלֹשָׁ֥ה לֵילֽוֹת׃ס

passages.text: Then David asked him, “To whom do you belong, and where are you from?” “I am an Egyptian,” he replied, “the slave of an Amalekite. My master abandoned me three days ago when I fell ill.
passages.sermon:
David spoke to the man.
David asked, “Who do you belong to?”
David also asked, “Where are you from?”
The man answered David.
He said, “I am an Egyptian.”
He said, “I am a young man.”
He said, “I am a slave.”
He said, “My master is an Amalekite.”
He said, “My master left me behind.”
He said, “He abandoned me three days ago.”
He said, “He left me because I became sick.”
passages.original: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר ל֤וֹ דָוִד֙ לְֽמִי־ אַ֔תָּה וְאֵ֥י מִזֶּ֖ה אָ֑תָּה וַיֹּ֜אמֶר נַ֧עַר מִצְרִ֣י אָנֹ֗כִי עֶ֚בֶד לְאִ֣ישׁ עֲמָֽלֵקִ֔י וַיַּעַזְבֵ֧נִי אֲדֹנִ֛י כִּ֥י חָלִ֖יתִי הַיּ֥וֹם שְׁלֹשָֽׁה׃

passages.text: We raided the Negev of the Cherethites, the territory of Judah, and the Negev of Caleb, and we burned down Ziklag.”
passages.sermon:
An Egyptian slave spoke to David.
He said, “We raided the Negev of the Cherethites.
We raided the territory of Judah.
We raided the Negev of Caleb.
We burned Ziklag with fire.”
passages.original: אֲנַ֡חְנוּ פָּשַׁ֜טְנוּ נֶ֧גֶב הַכְּרֵתִ֛י וְעַל־ אֲשֶׁ֥ר לִֽיהוּדָ֖ה וְעַל־ נֶ֣גֶב כָּלֵ֑ב וְאֶת־ צִקְלַ֖ג שָׂרַ֥פְנוּ בָאֵֽשׁ׃

passages.text: “Will you lead me to these raiders?” David asked. And the man replied, “Swear to me by God that you will not kill me or deliver me into the hand of my master, and I will lead you to them.”
passages.sermon:
David spoke to the Egyptian slave of an Amalekite.
David said, "Will you lead me to this band of raiders?"
The Egyptian slave answered David.
He said, "Swear to me by God."
He said, "Promise you will not kill me."
He said, "Promise you will not hand me over to my master."
He said, "If you swear, I will lead you to the raiders."
passages.original: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר אֵלָיו֙ דָּוִ֔ד הֲתוֹרִדֵ֖נִי אֶל־ הַגְּד֣וּד הַזֶּ֑ה וַיֹּ֡אמֶר הִשָּׁבְעָה֩ לִּ֨י בֵֽאלֹהִ֜ים אִם־ תְּמִיתֵ֗נִי וְאִם־ תַּסְגִּרֵ֙נִי֙ בְּיַד־ אֲדֹנִ֔י וְאוֹרִֽדְךָ֖ אֶל־ הַגְּד֥וּד הַזֶּֽה׃

passages.text: So he led David down, and there were the Amalekites spread out over all the land, eating, drinking, and celebrating the great amount of plunder they had taken from the land of the Philistines and the land of Judah.
passages.sermon:
The Amalekites were enemies of Israel.
They had raided the land of the Philistines and the land of Judah.
They took a great amount of plunder from these lands.
A man led David down to where the Amalekites were.
The Amalekites were spread out over all the land.
They were eating.
They were drinking.
They were celebrating.
They rejoiced over all the plunder they had taken.
passages.original: וַיֹּ֣רִדֵ֔הוּ וְהִנֵּ֥ה נְטֻשִׁ֖ים עַל־ פְּנֵ֣י כָל־ הָאָ֑רֶץ אֹכְלִ֤ים וְשֹׁתִים֙ וְחֹ֣גְגִ֔ים בְּכֹל֙ הַשָּׁלָ֣ל הַגָּד֔וֹל אֲשֶׁ֥ר לָקְח֛וּ מֵאֶ֥רֶץ פְּלִשְׁתִּ֖ים וּמֵאֶ֥רֶץ יְהוּדָֽה׃

passages.text: And David struck them down from twilight until the evening of the next day. Not a man escaped, except four hundred young men who fled, riding off on camels.
passages.sermon:
David was the leader of his men.
David attacked the Amalekites.
He began at twilight.
He continued fighting until the evening of the next day.
No Amalekite man escaped.
Only four hundred young men escaped.
These young men rode camels.
They fled from David.
passages.original: וַיַּכֵּ֥ם דָּוִ֛ד מֵהַנֶּ֥שֶׁף וְעַד־ הָעֶ֖רֶב לְמָֽחֳרָתָ֑ם וְלֹֽא־ נִמְלַ֤ט מֵהֶם֙ אִ֔ישׁ כִּי֩ אִם־ אַרְבַּ֨ע מֵא֧וֹת אִֽישׁ־ נַ֛עַר אֲשֶׁר־ רָכְב֥וּ עַל־ הַגְּמַלִּ֖ים וַיָּנֻֽסוּ׃

passages.text: So David recovered everything the Amalekites had taken, including his two wives.
passages.sermon:
David was the leader of his men.
The Amalekites had taken many things from David and his people.
David rescued everything the Amalekites had taken.
David also rescued his two wives.
passages.original: וַיַּצֵּ֣ל דָּוִ֔ד אֵ֛ת כָּל־ אֲשֶׁ֥ר לָקְח֖וּ עֲמָלֵ֑ק וְאֶת־ שְׁתֵּ֥י נָשָׁ֖יו הִצִּ֥יל דָּוִֽד׃

passages.text: Nothing was missing, young or old, son or daughter, or any of the plunder the Amalekites had taken. David brought everything back.
passages.sermon:
David was the leader of his men.
The Amalekites had taken many things from David and his people.
They took young people.
They took old people.
They took sons.
They took daughters.
They took all the plunder.
David brought everything back.
Nothing was missing.
passages.original: וְלֹ֣א נֶעְדַּר־ לָ֠הֶם מִן־ הַקָּטֹ֨ן וְעַד־ הַגָּד֜וֹל וְעַד־ בָּנִ֤ים וּבָנוֹת֙ וּמִשָּׁלָ֔ל וְעַ֛ד כָּל־ אֲשֶׁ֥ר לָקְח֖וּ לָהֶ֑ם הַכֹּ֖ל הֵשִׁ֥יב דָּוִֽד׃

passages.text: And he recovered all the flocks and herds, which his men drove ahead of the other livestock, calling out, “This is David’s plunder!”
passages.sermon:
David was the leader of his men.
David took all the sheep and cattle.
His men drove these animals in front of the other livestock.
The men said, “This is David’s plunder.”
passages.original: וַיִּקַּ֣ח דָּוִ֔ד אֶת־ כָּל־ הַצֹּ֖אן וְהַבָּקָ֑ר נָהֲג֗וּ לִפְנֵי֙ הַמִּקְנֶ֣ה הַה֔וּא וַיֹּ֣אמְר֔וּ זֶ֖ה שְׁלַ֥ל דָּוִֽד׃

passages.text: When David came to the two hundred men who had been too exhausted to follow him from the Brook of Besor, they came out to meet him and the troops with him. As David approached the men, he greeted them, but all the wicked and worthless men among those who had gone with David said, “Because they did not go with us, we will not share with them the plunder we recovered, except for each man’s wife and children. They may take them and go.”
passages.sermon:
David was the leader of the people.
Two hundred men had stayed behind at the Brook of Besor.
These men were too exhausted to continue with David.
David returned to these two hundred men.
The men who stayed behind came out to meet David.
They also came out to meet the people who were with David.
David approached these men.
David greeted them and asked about their well-being.
Some men had gone with David to the battle.
Among these men were wicked and worthless men.
These wicked men spoke up.
They said, “These men did not go with us.
We will not give them any of the plunder we recovered.
Each man may take only his wife and his children.
They may take them and go.”
passages.original: וַיָּבֹ֣א דָוִ֗ד אֶל־ מָאתַ֨יִם הָאֲנָשִׁ֜ים אֲשֶֽׁר־ פִּגְּר֣וּ׀ מִלֶּ֣כֶת׀ אַחֲרֵ֣י דָוִ֗ד וַיֹּֽשִׁיבֻם֙ בְּנַ֣חַל הַבְּשׂ֔וֹר וַיֵּֽצְאוּ֙ לִקְרַ֣את דָּוִ֔ד וְלִקְרַ֖את הָעָ֣ם אֲשֶׁר־ אִתּ֑וֹ וַיִּגַּ֤שׁ דָּוִד֙ אֶת־ הָעָ֔ם וַיִּשְׁאַ֥ל לָהֶ֖ם לְשָׁלֽוֹם׃ס וַיַּ֜עַן כָּל־ אִֽישׁ־ רָ֣ע וּבְלִיַּ֗עַל מֵֽהָאֲנָשִׁים֮ אֲשֶׁ֣ר הָלְכ֣וּ עִם־ דָּוִד֒ וַיֹּאמְר֗וּ יַ֚עַן אֲשֶׁ֣ר לֹֽא־ הָלְכ֣וּ עִמִּ֔י לֹֽא־ נִתֵּ֣ן לָהֶ֔ם מֵהַשָּׁלָ֖ל אֲשֶׁ֣ר הִצַּ֑לְנוּ כִּֽי־ אִם־ אִ֤ישׁ אֶת־ אִשְׁתּוֹ֙ וְאֶת־ בָּנָ֔יו וְיִנְהֲג֖וּ וְיֵלֵֽכוּ׃ס

passages.text: But David said, “My brothers, you must not do this with what the LORD has given us. He has protected us and delivered into our hands the raiders who came against us.
passages.sermon:
David was the leader of the men.
David spoke to his men.
He said, "My brothers, do not do this."
The LORD gave us these things.
The LORD protected us.
The LORD put the raiders who attacked us into our hands."
passages.original: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר דָּוִ֔ד לֹֽא־ תַעֲשׂ֥וּ כֵ֖ן אֶחָ֑י אֵ֠ת אֲשֶׁר־ נָתַ֨ן יְהוָ֥ה לָ֙נוּ֙ וַיִּשְׁמֹ֣ר אֹתָ֔נוּ וַיִּתֵּ֗ן אֶֽת־ הַגְּד֛וּד הַבָּ֥א עָלֵ֖ינוּ בְּיָדֵֽנוּ׃

passages.text: Who will listen to your proposal? The share of the one who went to battle will match the share of the one who stayed with the supplies. They will share alike.”
passages.sermon:
David was the leader of the men.
Some men went to battle with David.
Some men stayed behind to guard the supplies.
David spoke to the men who did not want to share the plunder.
David said, “No one will agree with your idea.
The one who went to battle will receive a share.
The one who stayed with the supplies will also receive a share.
They will all share alike.”
passages.original: וּמִי֙ יִשְׁמַ֣ע לָכֶ֔ם לַדָּבָ֖ר הַזֶּ֑ה כִּ֞י כְּחֵ֣לֶק׀ הַיֹּרֵ֣ד בַּמִּלְחָמָ֗ה וּֽכְחֵ֛לֶק הַיֹּשֵׁ֥ב עַל־ הַכֵּלִ֖ים יַחְדָּ֥ו יַחֲלֹֽקוּ׃ס

passages.text: And so it has been from that day forward. David established this statute as an ordinance for Israel to this very day.
passages.sermon:
David was the king of Israel.
David made a rule for Israel.
He established this rule on that day.
This rule became a law and a statute.
The rule has remained in Israel from that day until today.
passages.original: וַיְהִ֕י מֵֽהַיּ֥וֹם הַה֖וּא וָמָ֑עְלָה וַיְשִׂמֶ֜הָ לְחֹ֤ק וּלְמִשְׁפָּט֙ לְיִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל עַ֖ד הַיּ֥וֹם הַזֶּֽה׃פ

passages.text: When David arrived in Ziklag, he sent some of the plunder to his friends, the elders of Judah, saying, “Here is a gift for you from the plunder of the LORD’s enemies.”
passages.sermon:
David was the leader of his men.
David arrived in Ziklag.
He had plunder from battle.
He sent some of the plunder to his friends.
His friends were the elders of Judah.
He sent the plunder as a gift.
He said, “Here is a gift for you.”
He said, “This gift is from the plunder of the LORD’s enemies.”
passages.original: וַיָּבֹ֤א דָוִד֙ אֶל־ צִ֣קְלַ֔ג וַיְשַׁלַּ֧ח מֵֽהַשָּׁלָ֛ל לְזִקְנֵ֥י יְהוּדָ֖ה לְרֵעֵ֣הוּ לֵאמֹ֑ר הִנֵּ֤ה לָכֶם֙ בְּרָכָ֔ה מִשְּׁלַ֖ל אֹיְבֵ֥י יְהוָֽה׃

passages.text: He sent gifts to those in Bethel, Ramoth Negev, and Jattir; to those in Aroer, Siphmoth, and Eshtemoa; to those in Racal and in the cities of the Jerahmeelites and Kenites; to those in Hormah, Bor-ashan, and Athach; and to those in Hebron and in all the places where David and his men had roamed.
passages.sermon:
David was the leader of his men.
David sent gifts to many places.
He sent gifts to those in Bethel.
He sent gifts to those in Ramoth Negev.
He sent gifts to those in Jattir.
He sent gifts to those in Aroer.
He sent gifts to those in Siphmoth.
He sent gifts to those in Eshtemoa.
He sent gifts to those in Racal.
He sent gifts to those in the cities of the Jerahmeelites.
He sent gifts to those in the cities of the Kenites.
He sent gifts to those in Hormah.
He sent gifts to those in Bor-ashan.
He sent gifts to those in Athach.
He sent gifts to those in Hebron.
He sent gifts to all the places where he and his men had traveled.
passages.original: לַאֲשֶׁ֧ר בְּבֵֽית־ אֵ֛ל וְלַאֲשֶׁ֥ר בְּרָמֽוֹת־ נֶ֖גֶב וְלַאֲשֶׁ֥ר בְּיַתִּֽר׃ וְלַאֲשֶׁ֧ר בַּעֲרֹעֵ֛ר וְלַאֲשֶׁ֥ר בְּשִֽׂפְמ֖וֹת וְלַאֲשֶׁ֥ר בְּאֶשְׁתְּמֹֽעַ׃ס וְלַאֲשֶׁ֣ר בְּרָכָ֗ל וְלַֽאֲשֶׁר֙ בְּעָרֵ֣י הַיְּרַחְמְאֵלִ֔י וְלַאֲשֶׁ֖ר בְּעָרֵ֥י הַקֵּינִֽי׃ וְלַאֲשֶׁ֧ר בְּחָרְמָ֛ה וְלַאֲשֶׁ֥ר בְּבוֹר־ עָשָׁ֖ן וְלַאֲשֶׁ֥ר בַּעֲתָֽךְ׃ וְלַאֲשֶׁ֖ר בְּחֶבְר֑וֹן וּֽלְכָל־ הַמְּקֹמ֛וֹת אֲשֶֽׁר־ הִתְהַלֶּךְ־ שָׁ֥ם דָּוִ֖ד ה֥וּא וַאֲנָשָֽׁיו׃פ
